context:
Goal: a stalled background job never goes unnoticed, at a stated cost.
Problem (rule): rule outcomes-mechanize-rules bars a timer and a new long-lived process, and the stall-watch record says it adds none, but the hook runs one.
Based on (read): docs/decisions/stall-watch.md:65 says "no new process or timer".
Based on (read): hooks/stall_watch.py:20-26 runs a watcher per background job with a 0.2 s loop, reading BEAT on each pass.
Based on (read): no record grants stall-watch an exception.
Departs from: main, where the record misstates its cost — records an exception, or changes the hook.

options.gain: The stall alarm keeps working; the record tells the truth.
options.how: Rewrite stall-watch's cost line: one watcher process per background job, ending with its job, 0.2 s loop. Name it as your exception to outcomes-mechanize-rules.
options.label: Record an exception with its cost
options.lose: One small process per background job stays, as an exception to a rule.

options.gain: No timer or extra process anywhere; the rule holds with no exception.
options.how: Drop the watcher. The Stop check reads each job's log age once, when the session stops.
options.label: Rework to read on demand
options.lose: A stall is noticed only at the next Stop, not while the job runs.

ref: deep audit 1102, report docs/plans/deep-audit/report.md on audit/deep-1102 (6b6a41f3), table 'claude-settings: homes', row stall-watch-timer-rule
title: The stall watcher runs a looping process per background job, against the no-timer rule: grant an exception or rework it?
why: The watcher ends with its job, and a stall caught only at Stop loses the time the alarm exists to save.
